title: Update README.md to remove orchestrator references
Compare staging vs production sentiment accuracy
description:
Compare staging vs production sentiment accuracy — RESOLVED.

## Root Cause
A/B test on 2,737 live firehose posts proved replies are the primary driver of sentiment divergence. Staging was filtering replies; production was not.

## A/B Test Results (2025-02-08)
| Metric | Root only (staging) | All incl. replies (prod) | Replies only |
|--------|---|---|---|
| Count | 1,275 | 2,737 | 1,462 |
| Mean compound | +0.0633 | +0.0936 | +0.1200 |
| Net sentiment % | +6.3% | +9.4% | +12.0% |
| % Positive | 28.3% | 32.9% | 36.9% |
| % Negative | 17.6% | 17.5% | 17.4% |

Replies are 53% of English posts and skew +3pp more positive (support/agreement outweighs anger). Negative rate is identical across groups (~17.5%).

## Fixes Deployed (all to staging, 2025-02-08)
1. **Exclude unhydrated posts** — ghost posts with 0 engagement and no author were diluting sentiment (32012f6)
2. **Require explicit lang=en tag** — posts with no langs tag were assumed English, letting French/Spanish through VADER (fe62807)
3. **Include replies in analysis** — the primary divergence driver; aligns staging with production searchPosts behavior (23d22d8)

## Remaining Accepted Differences
- **Population selection bias**: Search API indexing lag vs real-time firehose means different post sets for same window. Inherent to architecture; expect bounded drift.
- **Minimum post threshold**: Production requires 1000+; staging has none. May adopt later if small-sample variance is an issue.
- **Deduplication strategy**: Production keeps highest-engagement duplicate; staging uses SQLite upsert. Low impact on sentiment.

title: Add minimum keyword match threshold for exemplar candidates
description:
## Problem

A post matching a single generic keyword (e.g. "canada") can be selected as an exemplar for any topic containing that keyword, even if the post has nothing to do with the topic. There is no minimum relevance floor.

## Proposed Fix

Add a HAVING clause or post-query filter requiring exemplar candidates to match at least one of:
- 2+ distinct keywords, OR
- 1+ compound keyword (containing underscore)

This acts as a safety floor — posts must demonstrate minimum relevance.

## Design Considerations

- Topics with very few keywords (2-3) may struggle to meet a 2-keyword threshold
- Need a fallback: if no candidate meets threshold, relax to 1-keyword match
- This is partially subsumed by Fix 2 (keyword weighting) — if compound terms are weighted 3x, single-generic-term matches naturally rank last
- Still valuable as defense-in-depth even with weighting

## Implementation

Option A — SQL HAVING:
```sql
GROUP BY pb.uri
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT je.value) >= 2
   OR MAX(CASE WHEN je.value LIKE '%[_]%' ESCAPE '[' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1
```

Option B — Go filter in exemplar.go after query:
- Filter candidates in Go, with automatic relaxation if filtered list is empty

## Files

- internal/store/topic_store.go (GetExemplarCandidates) OR internal/topics/exemplar.go (HydrateExemplars)
- Tests for threshold behavior and fallback

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Posts matching only 1 generic unigram are filtered out
- [ ] Posts matching 1 compound keyword pass the threshold
- [ ] Graceful fallback when no candidate meets threshold
- [ ] Test coverage for threshold filtering and fallback

title: SQLite read/write connection pool split to eliminate SQLITE_BUSY contention
description:
## Problem
Production and staging suffer from persistent SQLITE_BUSY (error 5) contention. Staging logs show 15+ consecutive cursor save failures over 12 minutes, a failed topic analysis cycle, and ~990 dropped firehose posts in a single incident window.

## Root Cause
Four concurrent write paths fight over SQLite's single write lock:
1. Write buffer flusher (500 posts + tokens in one tx, every 500ms)
2. Cursor saves (~every 48s from Jetstream consumer) 
3. Topic purge (1000-row DELETE batches)
4. Hydration updates (30-min burst of UPDATEs)

All share a 2-connection pool (store.go:128). When FlushWriteBatch holds a long tx, everything else gets SQLITE_BUSY.

## Solution
Split Store into separate read and write sql.DB pools:
- Write pool: MaxOpenConns(1) — serializes all writes at Go level, no SQLite-level contention
- Read pool: MaxOpenConns(4) — WAL allows unlimited concurrent readers

## Files to Change
- internal/store/store.go — Add writeDB field, open second connection, route writes to writeDB
- All Store write methods — Use s.writeDB instead of s.db for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/tx

## Acceptance Criteria
- All writes use the dedicated write connection
- All reads use the read pool
- No SQLITE_BUSY errors under staging firehose load
- Existing tests pass

title: Parallelize topic analysis with hydration/sparkline pipeline
description:
The trending topics post arrives 18-35s after the sparkline because the entire analysis cycle is sequential: hydrate → sentiment → summary → sparkline → TF-IDF → Gemini API → exemplars → trending post. The Gemini 2.5 Pro call alone takes 15-30s (with thinkingBudget:1024) and doesn't even start until the sparkline finishes uploading.

RunAnalysisCycle reads from topic_tokens (written by Jetstream at ingestion) — it has zero dependency on hydration, sentiment, or the Bluesky client. It can start as a goroutine at the top of runAnalysisCycle() and overlap entirely with the hydration+summary+sparkline pipeline.

Additionally, exemplar hydration runs 5 sequential DB queries (one per topic) that are independent and can run concurrently.

## Current sequential timeline (typical / worst)

| Step                              | Typical | Worst |
|-----------------------------------|---------|-------|
| Hydration (Bluesky API, 8.33rps) | 15s     | 60s   |
| Sentiment + summary post          | 2s      | 5s    |
| Sparkline generate + post         | 3s      | 8s    |
| RunAnalysisCycle (TF-IDF+Gemini)  | 15s     | 30s   |
| RunTrendingPost (exemplars+post)  | 3s      | 5s    |
| **Sparkline→topic gap**           | **18s** | **35s+** |

## Proposed parallel timeline

Start RunAnalysisCycle goroutine immediately, overlap with hydration+sparkline:

```
┌─ RunAnalysisCycle (TF-IDF + Gemini) ──── 15-30s ──┐
│                                                     │
├─ Hydrate (Bluesky API) ────── 15-60s ──┐           │
│  Sentiment + summary ── 2-5s ──┐       │           │
│  Sparkline gen+post ── 3-8s ───┤       │           │
│                                 ↓       ↓           ↓
│                              sparkline  (topic analysis already done)
│                              visible    
│                                         RunTrendingPost ── 3-5s
│                                         (exemplars + format + post)
```

With parallel exemplar queries, RunTrendingPost drops from 3-5s to 1-3s.

## Estimated savings

Sparkline→topic gap: 18-35s → 1-5s (saving 15-30s)
Total cycle time: unchanged (same work, just overlapped)

In the typical case, topic analysis (15-20s) finishes before hydration (15-60s) even completes — the gap becomes just RunTrendingPost formatting and posting.
close_reason: Implemented: parallel topic analysis goroutine + parallel exemplar hydration + timing instrumentation

title: Add SQLITE_BUSY retry helper and apply to SaveCursor and purgeInChunks
description:
## Problem  
SaveCursor (cursor.go) has zero retry logic — a single SQLITE_BUSY means the cursor is lost, risking firehose replay on crash. purgeInChunks (store.go) also fails entirely on first SQLITE_BUSY, killing the topic analysis cycle.

## Evidence
Staging logs: 15 consecutive 'save cursor: database is locked (5) (SQLITE_BUSY)' over 12 minutes. Topic analysis cycle failed: 'purge tokens: purge topic_tokens: database is locked (5) (SQLITE_BUSY)'.

## Solution
1. Create a withRetry helper: 3 attempts, exponential backoff (100ms, 500ms, 1s)
2. Apply to SaveCursor — cursor is critical, must not silently fail
3. Apply to purgeInChunks — retry individual chunks, not the whole operation
4. Log retry attempts at WARN level for observability

## Files to Change
- internal/store/store.go — Add withRetry helper function
- internal/store/cursor.go — Wrap SaveCursor exec in withRetry  
- internal/store/store.go purgeInChunks — Add per-chunk retry

## Acceptance Criteria
- SaveCursor retries up to 3 times on SQLITE_BUSY
- purgeInChunks retries each chunk up to 3 times  
- Retry attempts logged at WARN level
- Non-SQLITE_BUSY errors still fail immediately

title: Add Gemini semantic validation for exemplar post selection
description:
## Problem

Keyword-based exemplar matching is inherently imprecise — even with weighting and thresholds, a post can match topic keywords without actually being about the topic. A semantic validation step would catch these edge cases.

## Proposed Fix

After HydrateExemplars selects the top candidate per topic, batch-validate all 5 topic+post pairs in a single Gemini call. For any rejected pair, fall back to the next candidate.

## Design

### Prompt structure (single batched call):
Send 5 pairs of (topic_label, post_text) and ask Gemini to return a boolean per pair:
"For each pair, does the post meaningfully relate to the topic? Return JSON array of booleans."

### Rate limit impact:
- Current: ~96 calls/day (GroupAndLabel + GenerateAltText × 48 cycles)
- This adds: +48 calls/day (1 batched call per cycle)
- Total: ~144/day → bump maxDailyCalls from 100 to 150
- Dollar cost: ~$3/month (tiny input/output tokens)

### Latency:
- +2-5s per cycle (trivial vs current ~305s cycle time)

### Failure handling:
- If Gemini call fails → skip validation, use keyword-selected exemplar (fail-open)
- If ALL candidates rejected → use best keyword match anyway with logging

### Post text retrieval:
- Exemplar candidates already have URIs → need to join post_buffer for text
- Add text field to ExemplarCandidate struct, populate from post_buffer.text in the SQL query

## Files

- internal/topics/exemplar.go (add validation step after selection)
- internal/topics/grouper.go (add ValidateExemplars method, bump maxDailyCalls)
- internal/store/topic_store.go (add text to ExemplarCandidate + SQL query)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Batched Gemini validation call after exemplar selection
- [ ] Rejected exemplars replaced with next candidate
- [ ] Graceful fail-open on API errors
- [ ] Rate limit bumped to accommodate extra call
- [ ] Logging for rejected/accepted validations
- [ ] Test coverage for validation flow and fallbacks

title: Weight compound keywords higher in exemplar candidate ranking
description:
## Problem

GetExemplarCandidates (topic_store.go:138-148) ranks candidates by COUNT(DISTINCT je.value) — treating all keyword matches equally. A post matching 3 generic unigrams (canada, ice, olympics) outranks one matching 1 highly-specific compound term (jordan_binnington). This causes off-topic exemplar selection.

## Current SQL

```sql
ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT je.value) DESC, eng DESC
```

## Proposed Fix

Weight compound terms (bigrams containing underscore) higher than unigrams in the ranking:

Option A — SQL weighting:
```sql
ORDER BY SUM(CASE WHEN je.value LIKE '%[_]%' ESCAPE '[' THEN 3 ELSE 1 END) DESC, eng DESC
```

Option B — Two-tier approach: First prefer posts matching ANY compound keyword, then sort by distinct count + engagement within each tier.

Option C — Normalize by keyword set size: `COUNT(DISTINCT je.value) / total_keywords_in_topic` gives a relevance percentage. A post matching 2/3 keywords is better than one matching 3/15.

## Design Considerations

- Compound terms (jordan_binnington, super_bowl) are almost always topic-defining
- Single-word terms (canada, ice, hockey) are often contextual/ambiguous
- The 3:1 weight ratio needs tuning — could start conservative and adjust
- Must not break the existing relevance-beats-engagement test (topic_store_test.go:132)

## Files

- internal/store/topic_store.go (GetExemplarCandidates SQL, line 138-148)
- internal/store/topic_store_test.go (existing tests + new specificity test)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Compound keyword matches weighted higher than unigram matches
- [ ] Post matching jordan_binnington beats post matching canada+ice+olympics
- [ ] Existing tests pass (RelevanceBeatsEngagement, RankedByEngagement)
- [ ] New test: compound keyword specificity vs multiple unigram matches

title: Chart rendering improvements
description: Improve sparkline and yearly chart visual quality based on design review of graph-lab output. Six targeted fixes across both chart types.

title: Fix yearly X-axis month/date label collision
description:
CRITICAL. In yearly_generator.go, month name labels (drawYearlyMonthMarkers, y+height+15) collide with rotated biweekly date labels (drawYearlyBiweeklyTicks, y+height+25). The two label systems render on top of each other.

Fix: Remove the biweekly date text labels entirely. Keep only the short biweekly tick marks (the vertical lines at the bottom of the chart). Month names at y+height+15 become the sole text labels on the X-axis. Weekly ticks remain as-is (no text). Start/end date labels at y+height+50 remain.

Affected functions:

- drawYearlyMonthMarkers (line ~501): no change needed
- drawYearlyWeeklyTicks (line ~645): no change needed
- drawYearlyStartEndLabels (line ~710): no change needed

Validate: Run make graph-lab-yearly and visually confirm no label overlap in all 5 yearly scenarios.

title: Round Y-axis to nice numbers (both charts)
description:
Both sparkline and yearly charts show raw calculated Y-axis bounds (e.g. -8.1%, 24.2%) instead of clean rounded values (-10%, 25%).

Fix: Implement a niceNumber() utility function that rounds axis bounds outward to visually clean intervals. Algorithm (Heckbert's nice numbers):
1. Given data min/max, calculate the range
2. Pick a 'nice' tick spacing from {1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 25, 50} scaled to the range magnitude
3. Round min down and max up to the nearest tick multiple
4. Update labels to show the rounded values

Apply to:
- generator.go calculateYRange(): round finalMin down, finalMax up to nice intervals before returning
- yearly_generator.go calculateYearlyYRange(): same treatment
- drawLabels / drawYearlyLabels: display the rounded values instead of raw floats

Create a shared helper in a new file internal/sparkline/axis.go (or add to generator.go) with niceNumber(value float64, round bool) float64 and niceRange(min, max float64) (niceMin, niceMax float64).

Validate: Run make graph-lab, confirm all 10 charts show round Y-axis numbers (e.g. -10%, 0%, 10%, 25%, not -8.1%, 24.2%).

title: Add intermediate X-axis time labels to 48-hour sparkline
description:
The 48-hour sparkline only shows start and end times on the X-axis. No intermediate labels, making it impossible to locate mid-chart events.

Fix: The existing drawDayMarkers function already draws midnight UTC vertical lines with day labels for multi-day data. Enhance it to also add 6-hour or 12-hour intermediate tick marks with time labels.

In generator.go drawLabels():
- The multi-day branch (timeRange >= 1 day) already calls drawDayMarkers. Add additional hour markers at 06:00, 12:00, 18:00 UTC with smaller font/lighter color.
- The same-day branch shows only start/end labels. Add midpoint label.

Keep the midnight day labels (Mon, Tue etc.) as the primary markers. The hour labels should be secondary (smaller font, lighter color, shorter tick lines).

Validate: Run make graph-lab-sparkline, confirm all 5 sparkline scenarios have readable intermediate time references.

title: Reduce yearly X-axis tick density
description:
After fixing the label collision (gjw.1), the yearly charts still have too many vertical tick marks at the bottom. The combination of monthly + biweekly + weekly ticks creates visual noise.

Fix: Remove the weekly ticks entirely (drawYearlyWeeklyTicks). Keep only monthly grid lines (full height) and biweekly tick marks (short lines, no text per gjw.1). This gives a cleaner bottom edge.

In yearly_generator.go:
- Remove the call to drawYearlyWeeklyTicks from drawYearlyLabels (line ~468)
- Optionally remove the drawYearlyWeeklyTicks and findYearlyWeeklyPositions functions, or keep them for future use

Validate: Run make graph-lab-yearly, confirm the bottom edge of all 5 yearly charts looks cleaner with fewer tick marks.

title: Boost zone watermark contrast (both charts)
description:
The 'Positive', 'Neutral', 'Negative' background text watermarks are nearly invisible in all charts due to extremely low alpha values.

Current values:
- Neutral zone: color.RGBA{200, 200, 200, 30} (alpha 30/255 = 12% opacity)
- Positive: color.RGBA{40, 167, 69, 60} (alpha 60/255 = 24% opacity)
- Negative: color.RGBA{220, 53, 69, 60} (alpha 60/255 = 24% opacity)

Fix: Increase alpha values to make the text readable but still clearly 'background':
- Neutral: alpha 30 -> 60
- Positive: alpha 60 -> 100
- Negative: alpha 60 -> 100

Apply to both files:
- generator.go drawNeutralWatermark (line ~265), drawSentimentWatermarks (lines ~301, ~316)
- yearly_generator.go drawYearlyNeutralWatermark (line ~261), drawYearlySentimentWatermarks (lines ~289, ~302)

Validate: Run make graph-lab, confirm zone labels are legible but not distracting in all 10 charts.

title: Improve yearly trend line contrast over green data
description:
The blue dashed Gaussian trend line (color.RGBA{0, 123, 255, 255}) loses visibility when overlapping green positive data segments (color.RGBA{40, 167, 69, 255}). Blue-on-green has poor contrast.

Fix options (pick one):
A) Draw a white 'halo' behind the trend line: render the trend line twice — first pass with white color and thicker width (e.g. 3.5px), second pass with blue at 1.5px. This creates an outline effect.
B) Change the trend line color to something that contrasts with both green and red, such as dark purple (color.RGBA{100, 50, 150, 255}) or dark teal.
C) Use a solid (non-dashed) line with lower opacity for the trend.

Option A (white halo) is recommended as it preserves the current blue color identity while ensuring visibility over any data color.

Apply to:
- yearly_generator.go drawYearlyGaussianTrendLine (line ~896)
- generator.go drawGaussianTrendLine (line ~733) — apply same treatment for consistency

Jetstream Fly.io Bot: Full reimplementation on Fly.io with Jetstream
description:
## Goal

Reimplement hourstats-bsky as a Jetstream-based bot running on Fly.io for $5/month. Single Go binary with SQLite, achieving 100% post coverage (vs current ~10% via search API).

## Staging Account

All development and testing uses the staging Bluesky account:
- Handle: hourstats-staging.bsky.social
- Credentials: STAGING_BLUESKY_HANDLE and STAGING_BLUESKY_PASSWORD from .env

## Architecture

Single Go binary on Fly.io (shared-cpu-1x, 256MB) running:
- Jetstream WebSocket consumer (goroutine)
- 30-minute cron scheduler (goroutine)
- Window trigger + engagement hydration
- Processor (VADER sentiment + top-5 selection + Bluesky posting)
- Sparkline poster (7-day chart as reply)
- Daily aggregator
- Yearly poster
- SQLite on persistent volume (buffer + state + sentiment history)

## Key Specs

- Jetstream endpoint: wss://jetstream2.us-east.bsky.network/subscribe?wantedCollections=app.bsky.feed.post
- Post buffer: SQLite with 2-hour TTL
- Hydration: app.bsky.feed.getPosts (25 URIs/batch, 10 concurrent, rate limited)
- Sentiment: VADER (govader) with keyword fallback, thresholds ±0.3
- Mood vocabulary: 100 words across 7 tiers
- Charts: fogleman/gg (1200x800 sparkline, 1500x1000 yearly)
- Target: $5/month Fly.io Hobby plan

## Reference Documents

- openspec/changes/jetstream-migration/GREENFIELD_SPEC.md (full specification)
- openspec/changes/jetstream-migration/COST_ANALYSIS.md (cost analysis)
- openspec/changes/jetstream-migration/design.md (migration design)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Bot posts sentiment summaries every 30 minutes to staging account
- [ ] Sparkline chart posted as reply to each summary
- [ ] Daily aggregation runs at midnight UTC
- [ ] Yearly chart generation works
- [ ] Runs on Fly.io shared-cpu-1x 256MB within $5/month budget
- [ ] Cursor persistence survives restarts
- [ ] Consumer reconnects automatically on failure
close_reason: Migration complete; production running on Fly.io with Jetstream

title: Production cutover: deploy Fly.io and disable Lambda
description:
## Production Cutover Checklist

### Pre-deploy (one-time)
- [ ] Set secrets on Fly.io prod:
  ```bash
  fly secrets set -a hourstats-prod \
    BLUESKY_HANDLE="hourstats.bsky.social" \
    BLUESKY_PASSWORD="<app-password>" \
    GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY="<gemini-key>" \
    AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="<key>" \
    AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="<secret>"
  ```
- [ ] Ensure volume exists: `fly volumes list -a hourstats-prod`
- [ ] Decide on historical data: either start fresh (recommended — staging has validated from-scratch startup) or seed via `fly ssh console -a hourstats-prod` and run the `import-dynamodb` binary with DynamoDB export files. Sparklines need ~7 days to populate; yearly chart needs ~7 daily data points.

### Phase 1: Deploy with DRY_RUN=true
- [ ] Temporarily set `DRY_RUN = "true"` in fly.prod.toml
- [ ] Deploy: `make deploy-prod`
- [ ] Watch logs — verify Jetstream connects, posts are ingested: `make fly-logs-prod`
- [ ] Wait for one 30-min analysis cycle to complete (check logs for "DRY_RUN: would post")
- [ ] Confirm trending analysis runs (check logs for topic snapshots)
- [ ] Verify S3 backup credentials work (check logs for backup success or wait for daily cycle)
- [ ] Verify database created: `fly ssh console -a hourstats-prod -C "ls -la /data/hourstats-prod.db"`

### Phase 2: Cut over
- [ ] Disable Lambda EventBridge rule:
  ```bash
  aws events disable-rule --name hourstats-schedule --region us-east-1
  ```
- [ ] Wait for any in-flight Lambda execution to finish (~5 min)
- [ ] Change `DRY_RUN = "false"` in fly.prod.toml (revert the Phase 1 change)
- [ ] Redeploy: `make deploy-prod`
- [ ] Monitor first sentiment posting cycle (up to 30 min)
- [ ] Monitor first trending posting cycle (up to 6h)

### Post-cutover validation
- [ ] Verify sentiment post appears on @hourstats.bsky.social
- [ ] Verify sparkline reply attaches correctly (may need ~7 days of data first)
- [ ] Verify trendline reply attaches correctly
- [ ] Verify trending post appears with correct exemplar links (up to 6h wait)
- [ ] Verify S3 backup runs (check next daily cycle at midnight UTC)
- [ ] Confirm no double-posting (Lambda EventBridge rule is disabled)
- [ ] Verify yearly chart posts at 01:00 UTC (posts daily, needs ≥7 days of daily_sentiment data)

### Rollback plan
If Fly.io fails within the first week:
1. Re-enable Lambda: `aws events enable-rule --name hourstats-schedule --region us-east-1`
2. Stop Fly.io posting: set `DRY_RUN = "true"` in fly.prod.toml and redeploy
3. **Caveat**: Lambda rollback depends on DynamoDB transient state (hourstats-state table). If TTL has expired run state rows, the Lambda pipeline may fail on its first cycle but self-heal on the next 30-min trigger. Sentiment history and daily sentiment tables are persistent and unaffected.

After 1 week of stable Fly.io operation, Lambda rollback is no longer practical — proceed to decommission AWS resources.

### Config reference
fly.prod.toml: shared-cpu-1x, 512MB RAM, SJC region, trending every 6h, analysis every 30min, S3 backup to hourstats-sqlite-backups (us-west-2) with 7-day retention.
close_reason: Production cutover complete; Fly.io is the live production environment

title: Split FlushWriteBatch into separate post and token transactions
description:
## Problem
FlushWriteBatch (write_batch.go) does posts + topic_tokens + token_postings all in ONE transaction. For 500 posts with tokens, this means thousands of INSERTs under a single lock hold, blocking all other writers for seconds.

## Evidence
Staging logs: batch_size=500 flush errors, 12+ minutes of cursor SQLITE_BUSY, topic analysis failures.

## Solution
Split into two transactions:
1. First tx: INSERT posts into post_buffer (fast, ~500 upserts)
2. Second tx: INSERT topic_tokens + token_postings (only for posts with tokens)

If token tx fails, posts are still saved. Lock hold time roughly halved.

## Files to Change
- internal/store/write_batch.go — Split FlushWriteBatch into FlushPostBatch + FlushTokenBatch
- cmd/hourstats/main.go runWriteFlusher — Call both, handle partial failures

## Acceptance Criteria
- Posts saved even if token insertion fails
- Each transaction holds lock for half the previous duration
- Existing write_batch_test.go passes

title: Store Gemini synonyms in topic_snapshots for exemplar search
description:
## Problem

Gemini returns both Keywords and Synonyms for each topic cluster, but only Keywords are stored in topic_snapshots (analyzer.go:117). When RunTrendingPost loads topics from snapshots to hydrate exemplars, Synonyms is always nil. This means HydrateExemplars (exemplar.go:46) searches with a smaller keyword set than RankTopics used for ranking, causing exemplar mismatches.

## Root Cause

analyzer.go line 117:
```go
kwJSON, _ := json.Marshal(topic.Cluster.Keywords)  // Synonyms discarded
```

RunTrendingPost (analyzer.go:148-152) reconstructs TopicCluster without Synonyms:
```go
Cluster: TopicCluster{Label: s.Label, Description: s.Description, Keywords: kws, IsMeme: s.IsMeme}
```

## Evidence

Prod logs show exemplar for "Jordan Binnington" (hockey) was a curling post — broad keywords matched without synonyms to disambiguate.

## Fix

1. Add `synonyms TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` column to topic_snapshots (ALTER TABLE migration in store.go)
2. Store synonym JSON in InsertTopicSnapshot (topic_store.go:168)
3. Load synonyms in GetTopicSnapshotsSince (topic_store.go:184)
4. Populate TopicCluster.Synonyms when rebuilding from snapshots in RunTrendingPost (analyzer.go:148-152)

## Files

- internal/store/store.go (schema migration)
- internal/store/topic_store.go (InsertTopicSnapshot, GetTopicSnapshotsSince, GetRecentTopicSnapshots, TopicSnapshotRow)
- internal/topics/analyzer.go (RunAnalysisCycle line 117, RunTrendingPost line 148)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Synonyms stored and loaded from topic_snapshots
- [ ] HydrateExemplars receives non-nil Synonyms
- [ ] Old rows without synonyms handled gracefully (empty string default)
- [ ] Existing tests pass, new test for synonym round-trip
